questions.q: Which group sang 'Weak'?
questions.f: SWV stood for Sisters With Voices. 'Weak' reached #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1993.

questions.q: Boyz II Men's 'End of the Road' spent a record-breaking how many weeks at #1 on the Billboard Hot 100?
questions.f: 'End of the Road' spent 13 weeks at #1 in 1992.

questions.q: Which female R&B artist released the hit 'I Will Always Love You' as a cover in 1992?
questions.f: Originally written and recorded by Dolly Parton in 1973. Whitney's version spent 14 weeks at #1.

questions.q: R. Kelly's 'I Believe I Can Fly' was featured on the soundtrack of which 1996 film?
questions.f: 'I Believe I Can Fly' won three Grammy Awards in 1998.

questions.q: TLC's 'Waterfalls' spent how many weeks at #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1995?
questions.f: 'Waterfalls' was TLC's biggest chart hit, spending 7 weeks at #1.

questions.q: Brandy and Monica's chart-topping duet 'The Boy Is Mine' won which Grammy Award at the 41st ceremony in 1999?
c: Best R&B Vocal Performance by a Duo or Group
questions.f: 'The Boy Is Mine' won Best R&B Vocal Performance by a Duo or Group at the 41st Grammy Awards in 1999. The song spent 13 weeks at #1 on the Hot 100 — tying the then-record held by Boyz II Men's 'End of the Road.'

questions.q: Who sang the 1994 hit 'Always Be My Baby'?
Which R&B group released 'Waterfalls' in 1995?
Salt-N-Pepa's 'Shoop' appeared on which 1993 album?
c: A Salt with a Deadly Pepa

questions.q: Which artist had a 1993 hit with 'That's the Way Love Goes'?
Who produced Ginuwine's debut hit 'Pony' (1996)?
questions.f: Timbaland and Ginuwine had been childhood friends. 'Pony' launched both of their careers.

questions.q: Babyface co-wrote and produced 'Exhale (Shoop Shoop)' for which 1995 film soundtrack?
questions.f: Babyface produced the entire Waiting to Exhale soundtrack.

questions.q: Maxwell's debut album 'Maxwell's Urban Hang Suite' was released in what year?
questions.f: Maxwell's Urban Hang Suite is widely credited as one of the defining neo-soul albums of the 1990s.

questions.q: Keith Sweat helped pioneer the New Jack Swing era. Which label released his debut 'Make It Last Forever'?
questions.f: Keith Sweat's debut on Elektra in 1987 is considered one of the earliest New Jack Swing albums.

questions.q: Jodeci's 'Forever My Lady' appeared on which debut album released in 1991?
c: The Show the After Party the Hotel
questions.f: Jodeci's debut album Forever My Lady went triple platinum.

questions.q: Missy Elliott's debut album 'Supa Dupa Fly' was released in what year?
Which producer is credited on Mary J. Blige's 'Real Love' from What's the 411?
Toni Braxton's self-titled debut album was released on which label?
D'Angelo's 'Brown Sugar' debut album was released on which record label in 1995?
questions.f: Brown Sugar was released on EMI Records on July 3, 1995.

questions.q: Before solo stardom, which member of 702 was originally from Las Vegas and lead vocalist on 'Steelo'?
questions.f: 702 were originally from Las Vegas and were discovered after winning a talent contest.

questions.q: Erykah Badu's debut single 'On & On' appeared on which 1997 album?
Which city's music scene did Organized Noize help define with their production work for OutKast and TLC?
Puff Daddy and Faith Evans' 1997 hit 'I'll Be Missing You' was a tribute to which rapper?
questions.f: 'I'll Be Missing You' debuted at #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 and spent 11 weeks at the top in 1997.

questions.q: Blackstreet's 1996 smash 'No Diggity' featured which rapper on the track?
questions.f: 'No Diggity' spent four weeks at #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 and won Best R&B Performance by a Duo or Group at the 1997 Grammys.

questions.q: Destiny's Child's debut single 'No No No Part 2' (1997) was remixed by which Fugee?
questions.f: Wyclef Jean's remix of 'No No No' transformed Destiny's Child's debut into a top 10 R&B hit in 1997.

questions.q: Which rapper duetted with Mary J. Blige on the 1995 hit 'You're All I Need to Get By'?
questions.f: 'You're All I Need to Get By' reached #1 on the Billboard Hot R&B Singles chart in 1995 and earned a Grammy for Best Rap Duo or Group Performance.

questions.q: Pras Michel's 1998 hit 'Ghetto Supastar (That Is What You Are)' featured Mýa alongside which rapper?
questions.f: 'Ghetto Supastar' appeared on the Bulworth film soundtrack and reached the top 5 in multiple countries including the UK.

questions.q: Eric Benét's 1999 R&B ballad 'Spend My Life with You' featured which Canadian singer?
questions.f: 'Spend My Life with You' reached #1 on the Billboard R&B chart and was nominated for Best R&B Performance by a Duo or Group at the 2000 Grammys.

questions.q: Mýa's self-titled debut album was released in what year?
Tamia's debut single 'You Put a Move on My Heart' (1995) appeared on which film's soundtrack?
Faith Evans and The Notorious B.I.G., who married in 1994, were both signed to which record label?
Before his solo career, Pras Michel was a member of which group?
Before forming Blackstreet, Teddy Riley co-founded which earlier New Jack Swing group?
questions.f: Guy's debut 'The Future' (1988) is credited as one of the first albums to fully define the New Jack Swing sound.

questions.q: Jermaine Dupri produced Usher's 1997 commercial breakthrough album. What was it called?
questions.f: Jermaine Dupri's production on 'My Way' yielded the hit 'You Make Me Wanna...' — Usher's first top 5 pop crossover.

questions.q: Mariah Carey's 1995 megahit 'Fantasy' built its groove around a sample from 'Genius of Love' — a track originally recorded by which band?
questions.f: 'Fantasy' (1995) samples Tom Tom Club's 1981 hit 'Genius of Love' — building its euphoric groove on one of the most infectious basslines of the New Wave era. Tom Tom Club was a side project of Talking Heads members Chris Frantz and Tina Weymouth.

questions.q: LaFace Records — home to TLC, Usher, and Toni Braxton — was co-founded by Babyface and which other producer-executive?
questions.f: L.A. Reid and Babyface launched LaFace Records in 1989 with backing from Arista's Clive Davis.

questions.q: Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis produced Janet Jackson's 1997 album exploring personal themes of sexuality and mental health. Name that album.
questions.f: The Velvet Rope debuted at #1 in 14 countries upon its 1997 release and is widely considered Janet's most personal album.

questions.q: Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis began their long production partnership with Janet Jackson on which 1986 album?
Organized Noize were founding members of which Atlanta collective that also included OutKast and Goodie Mob?
Jermaine Dupri produced 'Totally Krossed Out,' the debut album by which pre-teen rap duo?
The 1998 song 'Take Me There' was performed by Blackstreet and Mýa as the lead track for which animated film's soundtrack?
questions.f: 'Take Me There' reached the top 20 on the Billboard Hot 100 and was the lead single from The Rugrats Movie soundtrack on Interscope Records.

questions.q: Gerald Levert's father Eddie Levert is the longtime lead singer of which soul group?
questions.f: Eddie Levert and Gerald Levert recorded together as Levert Sweat Gill and separately as 'Father and Son' — releasing a joint album in 1995.

questions.q: Before his 2000 solo breakout with 'Thong Song,' Sisqó was a lead vocalist in which R&B group?
Keith Sweat's 1996 hit 'Twisted' featured which R&B trio?
Boyz II Men's 'End of the Road' was recorded for which 1992 Eddie Murphy comedy?
questions.f: 'End of the Road' spent 13 weeks at #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 after its placement on the Boomerang soundtrack.

questions.q: Janet Jackson's 'Again' was written for which 1993 John Singleton film?
questions.f: 'Again' was nominated for an Academy Award for Best Original Song and peaked at #1 on the Billboard Hot 100.

questions.q: Warren G and Nate Dogg's 1994 hit 'Regulate' was the lead single from which film's soundtrack?
questions.f: 'Regulate' reached #2 on the Billboard Hot 100 and made Warren G and Nate Dogg household names on the strength of the Above the Rim placement.

questions.q: Which R&B vocalist delivered 'Not Gon' Cry' — the emotional centerpiece of the Waiting to Exhale (1995) soundtrack?
questions.f: Mary J. Blige's 'Not Gon' Cry' — written and produced by Babyface — became the defining track of the Waiting to Exhale soundtrack and one of the signature performances of her career.

questions.q: Maxwell's 'Sumthin' Sumthin'' was featured on which 1997 neo-soul film soundtrack?
questions.f: The Love Jones (1997) soundtrack is widely considered the defining neo-soul film record of the decade.

questions.q: Aaliyah's 'Are You That Somebody' appeared on the soundtrack of which 1998 Eddie Murphy comedy?
questions.f: 'Are You That Somebody' was produced by Timbaland and marked Aaliyah's creative rebirth after splitting from R. Kelly.

questions.q: Color Me Badd's debut hit 'I Wanna Sex You Up' appeared on which 1991 crime drama's soundtrack?
The 1997 drama Soul Food and its R&B soundtrack are set in which American city?
The Friday (1995) film soundtrack was released on which West Coast rap label?
Before her film career in movies like Set It Off and Chicago, Queen Latifah was known for which musical genre?
The Above the Rim (1994) Death Row soundtrack credits which label co-founder as executive producer?
questions.f: Above the Rim was one of Death Row's first major soundtrack releases, cementing the label's dominance over West Coast R&B and rap in 1994.

questions.q: New Jack City (1991) featured the song 'New Jack Hustler (Nino's Theme)' performed by which rapper?
questions.f: Ice-T also appeared in New Jack City as a detective, making him both a cast member and a soundtrack contributor on the same film.

questions.q: The Friday (1995) soundtrack was executive-produced by which rapper who also directed and starred in the film?
questions.f: Ice Cube wrote, directed, starred in, and executive-produced Friday — one of the most complete creative packages in 90s hip-hop cinema.

questions.q: The Waiting to Exhale (1995) soundtrack — with Babyface producing every track — was released on which label?
questions.f: The Waiting to Exhale soundtrack debuted at #1 on the Billboard 200 and spent three weeks at the top.

questions.q: Love Jones (1997) featured 'Hopeless' by Dionne Farris, who had previously been a vocalist with which group?
questions.f: Dionne Farris sang the hook on Arrested Development's Grammy-winning 'Tennessee' (1992) before launching her solo career.

questions.q: Tupac Shakur's contribution to the Above the Rim (1994) Death Row soundtrack was titled what?
Which female R&B group had a career-reviving US hit with 'Don't Let Go (Love)' from the Set It Off (1996) soundtrack?
Jason's Lyric (1994) featured a smooth R&B cover of the Japanese pop standard 'Sukiyaki' by which group?
The Set It Off (1996) soundtrack's collaborative ballad 'Missing You' featured Brandy, Tamia, Gladys Knight, and which fourth vocalist?
questions.f: 'Missing You' brought together four generations of Black female vocalists on a single film ballad.

questions.q: Diana King's 1995 R&B-reggae crossover hit 'Shy Guy' appeared on which action film's soundtrack?
questions.f: 'Shy Guy' gave Diana King a top 5 US hit entirely on the strength of its placement on the Bad Boys soundtrack.

questions.q: En Vogue's 'Don't Let Go (Love)' appeared on which 1996 film's soundtrack?
Color Me Badd — whose debut hit appeared on the New Jack City soundtrack — originally formed in which city?
Toni Braxton's 1996 power ballad 'Un-Break My Heart' was written by which songwriter?
questions.f: Diane Warren wrote 'Un-Break My Heart' as a straight pop record — Toni Braxton and producer Babyface transformed it into one of the defining R&B ballads of the decade.

questions.q: R. Kelly wrote and produced 'You Are Not Alone' — the 1995 #1 hit — for which artist?
questions.f: 'You Are Not Alone' became the first single ever to debut at #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 upon its release in 1995.

questions.q: Which artist co-wrote the majority of tracks on Aaliyah's 1996 album 'One in a Million'?
questions.f: Missy Elliott co-wrote several tracks on 'One in a Million' alongside Timbaland, marking the beginning of one of R&B's most celebrated creative partnerships.

questions.q: TLC's 1994 hit 'Creep' was written by which Atlanta-based songwriter-producer?
questions.f: Dallas Austin wrote and produced 'Creep' — it reached #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in early 1995.

questions.q: Babyface wrote 'Breathe Again' for which singer's self-titled 1993 debut album?
questions.f: 'Breathe Again' peaked at #3 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1994 and established Babyface's signature slow-burn ballad formula.

questions.q: R. Kelly ghostwrote and produced 'Down Low (Nobody Has to Know)' for which veteran soul group's 1996 comeback?
questions.f: 'Down Low (Nobody Has to Know)' reached #4 on the Billboard Hot 100 and revived the Isley Brothers' commercial relevance in the mid-90s.

questions.q: Mariah Carey co-wrote her 1993 hit 'Hero' with which songwriter-producer?
Babyface wrote Boyz II Men's 'On Bended Knee' — on which 1994 album did it appear?
Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis wrote 'Can You Stand the Rain' for which R&B group?
Before going solo, Missy Elliott signed her first record deal as a member of which mid-90s R&B group?
TLC's 1999 smash 'No Scrubs' was co-written by which member of Xscape?
questions.f: Kandi Burruss co-wrote 'No Scrubs' alongside Kevin 'She'kspere' Briggs — the writing credit became the foundation of her post-Xscape career.

questions.q: Which member of TLC is credited as co-writer on the group's 1994 hit 'Waterfalls'?
questions.f: Left Eye wrote the rap verse on 'Waterfalls' and holds a co-writing credit on the track alongside Organized Noize's production team.

questions.q: Missy Elliott wrote '4 Page Letter' — a standout track from the 1996 album 'One in a Million' — for which artist?
questions.f: '4 Page Letter' became one of Aaliyah's signature album cuts and helped cement Missy Elliott's reputation as a writer for other artists before her own solo debut.

questions.q: En Vogue's 1992 hit 'My Lovin' (You're Never Gonna Get It)' was written and produced by which songwriter duo?
questions.f: Denzil Foster and Thomas McElroy were the creative architects of En Vogue's entire early catalog — writing and producing across both their debut and Funky Divas.

questions.q: Which songwriter co-wrote New Edition's 1988 ballad 'Can You Stand the Rain' alongside his production partner Terry Lewis?
questions.f: 'Can You Stand the Rain' is widely cited as one of Jimmy Jam and Terry Lewis's most emotionally precise pieces of songwriting.

questions.q: Jimmy Jam co-wrote 'Can You Stand the Rain' for New Edition alongside which production partner?
LaShawn Daniels co-wrote Destiny's Child's 'Say My Name' — he also co-wrote which 1999 Whitney Houston hit?
c: It's Not Right But It's Okay

questions.q: Dallas Austin named his Atlanta production company after his own initials. What does DARP stand for?
Static Major co-wrote Ginuwine's 'Pony' alongside Timbaland. What was Static Major's real name?
questions.f: Stephen Garrett — known as Static Major — co-wrote 'Pony' and dozens of other Timbaland-era records before his death in 2008.

questions.q: Before his songwriting career, Static Major was a member of which late-90s R&B vocal group?
questions.f: Static Major was a founding member of Playa — the Def Jam R&B group whose album 'Cheers 2 U' (1998) laid the groundwork for his transition into songwriting and production.

questions.q: Playa — the R&B group Static Major belonged to — had a 1998 hit with which single?
Ginuwine — whose 'Pony' Static Major co-wrote — performs under which birth name?
Andre Harrell founded which New York-based label that was home to Mary J. Blige, Jodeci, and Heavy D?
questions.f: Uptown Records was founded by Andre Harrell in 1986 and became the defining label of New York hip-hop soul through the early 1990s.

questions.q: Jermaine Dupri founded which Atlanta-based label that launched Kris Kross, Xscape, and Da Brat?
questions.f: So So Def Recordings was founded in 1993 and distributed through Columbia, becoming one of Atlanta's most commercially dominant independent labels of the decade.

questions.q: Teddy Riley relocated from Harlem to which Virginia city to found Blackstreet and establish his recording studio?
questions.f: Teddy Riley's move to Virginia Beach in the early 1990s created a gravitational pull — Timbaland, Missy Elliott, and DeVante Swing all built careers in the same region within a few years.

questions.q: Jodeci formed in which Southern state before signing to Uptown Records in New York?
questions.f: The DeGrate and Hailey families both hailed from North Carolina — Jodeci were a Southern group that the New York Uptown sound transformed into an urban phenomenon.

questions.q: The Neptunes production duo consists of Pharrell Williams and which Virginia Beach co-producer?
questions.f: Chad Hugo and Pharrell Williams met as teenagers in Virginia Beach and formed The Neptunes — one of the most commercially dominant production duos of the late 90s and 2000s.

questions.q: Uptown Records flagship rapper Heavy D was born in which Caribbean country?
questions.f: Heavy D was born Dwight Arrington Myers in Mandeville, Jamaica, and immigrated to Mount Vernon, New York — his Jamaican roots informed the rhythmic swagger that defined his Uptown sound.

questions.q: Which music executive founded Uptown Records and later mentored Sean 'Puff Daddy' Combs?
Jodeci's four members originally formed in which North Carolina city?
André 3000 and Big Boi of OutKast first met as students at which Atlanta high school?
Uptown Records was distributed through which major label in the early 1990s?
Jodeci's primary songwriter and producer DeVante Swing performed under which birth name?
questions.f: Donald DeGrate — DeVante Swing — wrote and produced virtually all of Jodeci's catalog while simultaneously building a Virginia collective that would launch Timbaland and Missy Elliott.

questions.q: Before founding Uptown Records, Andre Harrell launched his career as one half of which hip-hop duo?
questions.f: As half of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde, Andre Harrell recorded for Profile Records in the early 1980s before transitioning into A&R and eventually founding Uptown.

questions.q: Jermaine Dupri famously discovered Kris Kross performing in which Atlanta shopping mall?
questions.f: Jermaine Dupri spotted Chris Kelly and Chris Smith performing at Greenbriar Mall in southwest Atlanta in 1991 — within a year they had a triple-platinum debut.

questions.q: Da Brat — signed to So So Def — became the first female solo rapper with a platinum-selling debut. What was that album called?
questions.f: Funkdafied (1994) went platinum, making Da Brat the first female solo rapper to achieve that milestone — on Jermaine Dupri's label, distributed out of Atlanta.

questions.q: DeVante Swing assembled Timbaland, Missy Elliott, and Static Major into which Virginia-based collective in the early 1990s?
questions.f: Swing Mob — assembled by DeVante Swing — was one of the most talent-dense collectives in 90s R&B, incubating artists who would each go on to define the next era of the genre.

questions.q: Pharrell Williams and Chad Hugo first connected through which Virginia arts program during high school?
c: The Governor's School for the Arts

questions.q: Before founding Uptown Records, Andre Harrell worked as an A&R executive at which rap label founded by Russell Simmons?
The Uptown Records sound — blending hip-hop production with R&B vocals — was known by which genre term Andre Harrell helped popularize?
DeVante Swing's Virginia collective — which incubated Timbaland and Missy Elliott — was also known by which alternate name?
questions.f: Da Bassment — also called Swing Mob — was a live-in creative compound in Virginia where DeVante Swing housed and developed artists including Timbaland, Missy Elliott, and Static Major throughout the early 1990s.

questions.q: Organized Noize recorded their landmark sessions with OutKast and TLC at which Atlanta studio?
questions.f: Bosstown Studios in Atlanta was the recording home of Organized Noize's most important work — including early OutKast sessions and TLC's CrazySexyCool production.

questions.q: Teddy Riley grew up in which New York neighborhood before relocating to Virginia Beach?
Jermaine Dupri's So So Def label was distributed through which major label throughout the 1990s?
'I Like the Way (The Kissing Game)' was the 1991 breakout smash for which R&B group?
questions.f: 'I Like the Way (The Kissing Game)' reached #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1991, making Hi-Five one of the most unlikely chart-toppers of the new jack swing era.

questions.q: 'Freak Me' was the 1993 chart-topping debut single for which R&B group?
questions.f: 'Freak Me' spent four weeks at #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1993 — Silk's commercial peak and the record that defined their career.

questions.q: Which duo had their only major US hit with 'Tell Me' in 1995, featuring vocalist Amel Larrieux?
questions.f: 'Tell Me' reached #7 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1995. Groove Theory never released a follow-up album, and Amel Larrieux eventually launched a solo career.

questions.q: 'Knockin' Da Boots' was the 1993 debut hit for which Texas-based R&B trio?
questions.f: 'Knockin' Da Boots' reached #3 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1993 and established H-Town as one of Houston's first R&B exports.

questions.q: 'Nobody Knows' was the 1996 breakout and commercial peak for which artist — a solo project named after its singer?
questions.f: 'Nobody Knows' peaked at #2 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1996 and won a Grammy for Best R&B Song. Tony Rich never replicated its commercial success.

questions.q: Which R&B harmony group peaked with 'If I Ever Fall in Love' in 1992 and never replicated that commercial success?
questions.f: 'If I Ever Fall in Love' reached #2 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1992 and was recorded almost entirely a cappella — a choice that became its defining characteristic.

questions.q: Zhané's 1994 debut single 'Hey Mr. DJ' appeared on which debut album?
Changing Faces — the duo behind 1994's 'Stroke You Up' — scored their debut hit on which label?
Hi-Five's lead vocalist on 'I Like the Way (The Kissing Game)' was which singer?
'If I Ever Fall in Love' by Shai was performed primarily in which vocal style — almost entirely without instruments?
Hi-Five — the group behind 'I Like the Way (The Kissing Game)' — came from which Texas city rarely associated with 90s R&B?
questions.f: Hi-Five formed in Waco, Texas — not a city associated with R&B infrastructure, label connections, or music industry access — which made their national breakthrough even more unlikely.

questions.q: Silk — the group behind 'Freak Me' — were developed and mentored by which New Edition alumnus?
questions.f: Michael Bivins discovered and developed Silk as part of his pattern of mentoring emerging R&B acts — he had already done the same for Boyz II Men and Another Bad Creation.

questions.q: Groove Theory vocalist Amel Larrieux eventually launched a solo career with which 2000 debut album?
questions.f: After Groove Theory went quiet, Amel Larrieux built a respected solo career entirely outside the mainstream — Infinite Possibilities is considered a quiet neo-soul classic.

questions.q: H-Town — the trio behind 'Knockin' Da Boots' — were from which Texas city?
questions.f: H-Town — brothers Keven 'Dino' Conner and Solomon 'Shazam' Conner, plus Darryl 'G' Jackson — were from Houston, making them part of the city's first wave of national R&B recognition.

questions.q: The R&B group Shai took their name from a word meaning 'gift' in which ancient language?
questions.f: Shai is a Hebrew word meaning 'gift' — the group chose the name while students at Howard University, connecting their identity to their academic and cultural environment.

questions.q: Michael Bivins — who mentored Silk — was a founding member of which New Edition alumni trio?
The Tony Rich Project's 'Nobody Knows' peaked at which position on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1996?
Zhané were signed to which major label for their debut album 'Pronounced Jah-Nay'?
Portrait — the four-man harmony group behind 1992's 'Here We Go Again' — were signed to which major label?
questions.f: Portrait's self-titled debut was released on Capitol Records in 1992 — the label pushed 'Here We Go Again' as their breakout single, and it remains the group's only significant chart entry.

questions.q: Shai formed while all four members were students at which historically Black university in Washington D.C.?
questions.f: All four members of Shai — Carl Martin, Marc Nelson, Darnell Van Rensalier, and Geoffrey Williams — met as students at Howard University, one of the most prominent HBCUs in the country.

questions.q: Portrait — whose 'Here We Go Again' was a 1992 R&B hit — were from which California city?
Shai's 1992 debut album shared its title with their breakthrough single. What was that title?
c: If I Ever Fall in Love

questions.q: SWV's 1992 hit 'Right Here (Human Nature Remix)' was built around an interpolation of which Michael Jackson song?
questions.f: 'Right Here (Human Nature Remix)' became SWV's breakthrough hit, interpolating Michael Jackson's 'Human Nature' from Thriller — the remix became more successful than the original version of 'Right Here.'

questions.q: Which producer dominated urban radio remix culture from 1993 to 1997 and became known as the architect of the Bad Boy remix sound?
questions.f: Puff Daddy's remix approach — dense samples, rap features, and radio-ready drum programming — defined how major labels used remixes as commercial tools through the mid-90s.

questions.q: The So So Def remix of TLC's 'Creep' — included on 'CrazySexyCool' — was produced by which Atlanta hitmaker?
questions.f: Jermaine Dupri's So So Def remix of 'Creep' appeared alongside Dallas Austin's original production on CrazySexyCool — a rare case of two competing versions appearing on the same album.

questions.q: Mary J. Blige's 'Real Love' remix featured which rapper — a member of Brand Nubian?
questions.f: Grand Puba's feature on the 'Real Love' remix was one of the defining moments of the hip-hop soul crossover — his Brand Nubian credibility lending the record street authority alongside Mary's vocals.

questions.q: Brandy's 'I Wanna Be Down (Human Rhythm Remix)' featured Queen Latifah, MC Lyte, and which third female rapper?
questions.f: The 'I Wanna Be Down' remix brought together four of the most prominent women in early 90s hip-hop and R&B on a single record — a deliberate statement about female solidarity in the genre.

questions.q: The 1994 global crossover 'Here Comes the Hotstepper' remix was produced by which producer who later worked with Nas and Amy Winehouse?
questions.f: Salaam Remi's remix of 'Here Comes the Hotstepper' reached #1 in the US and UK in 1994 — launching both Ini Kamoze's brief mainstream career and establishing Remi as a go-to remix architect.

questions.q: Craig Mack's 'Flava in Ya Ear' remix featured Notorious B.I.G., Busta Rhymes, and Rampage alongside which fourth rapper?
Mariah Carey's 1995 smash 'Fantasy (Remix)' sampled which Tom Tom Club song?
Brandy's 'I Wanna Be Down (Human Rhythm Remix)' appeared on which 1994 debut album?
The Salaam Remi remix of 'Here Comes the Hotstepper' was the lead single for which 1994 Robert Altman film's soundtrack?
New York remix production duo The Trackmasters consisted of Tone and which second producer?
questions.f: The Trackmasters — Tone (Ivan Matias) and Poke (Jean-Claude Olivier) — produced and remixed records for Nas, Will Smith, Jennifer Lopez, and dozens of others throughout the mid-to-late 90s.

questions.q: Mary J. Blige's 'I Can Love You' remix featured which rapper who was a founding member of Junior M.A.F.I.A.?
questions.f: 'I Can Love You' was one of several late-90s collaborations between Mary J. Blige and the Bad Boy orbit — Lil' Kim's Junior M.A.F.I.A. ties connecting both artists to the Brooklyn rap ecosystem.

questions.q: Mariah Carey released a remix EP following the success of 'Fantasy' — it was titled what?
questions.f: Daydream Interlude was released alongside Daydream and packaged as a companion remix project — one of the earliest major-label uses of a standalone remix EP as a commercial release strategy.

questions.q: The Trackmasters produced which 1996 Nas single — from his album 'It Was Written' — that became a remix staple on urban radio?
questions.f: 'Street Dreams' sampled Eurythmics' 'Sweet Dreams (Are Made of This)' and was produced by The Trackmasters — the combination of the sample flip and Nas's verse made it a crossover radio staple.

questions.q: The 1994 'Flava in Ya Ear' remix featured four rappers — which of the four released his debut album 'The Coming' two years later in 1996?
questions.f: Busta Rhymes stole the 'Flava in Ya Ear' remix with one of the most energetic verses of 1994 — two years later 'The Coming' debuted at #6 on the Billboard 200.

questions.q: Lil' Kim — who appeared on Mary J. Blige's remix — was a founding member of which rap group?
The Tom Tom Club — whose 'Genius of Love' was sampled in Mariah's 'Fantasy' remix — was a side project of musicians from which band?
Brandy's self-titled debut album — home to the 'I Wanna Be Down' remix — was released on which major label?
The 1992 Boyz II Men remix collection 'Cooleyhighharmony (Remix)' was produced entirely by which New Jack Swing architect?
questions.f: Teddy Riley's full-album remix of Cooleyhighharmony applied the New Jack Swing production template to Boyz II Men's already-successful debut — a rare case of a remix collection becoming as commercially significant as the original.

questions.q: The 'Always Be My Baby (Street Remix)' by Mariah Carey — produced by Jermaine Dupri — featured a guest verse from which So So Def artist?
questions.f: Jermaine Dupri produced the 'Always Be My Baby (Street Remix)' and brought Da Brat — his So So Def signee — onto the record, connecting Mariah's mainstream pop world to Atlanta's rap infrastructure.

questions.q: The Tom Tom Club's 'Genius of Love' — sampled in Mariah's 'Fantasy' remix — was originally released on which label?
Which production collective — responsible for Public Enemy's catalog — directly influenced Puff Daddy's dense sample-based remix approach?
Lauryn Hill won how many Grammy Awards at the 1999 ceremony for 'The Miseducation of Lauryn Hill'?
questions.f: Lauryn Hill's five Grammys at the 1999 ceremony set a record for the most won by a female artist in a single night — a record that stood for years.

questions.q: TLC won Grammy Best R&B Album for 'CrazySexyCool' at which numbered Grammy ceremony?
questions.f: TLC won Best R&B Album at the 38th Grammy Awards in 1996 for CrazySexyCool — one of four Grammy nominations the album received.

questions.q: Whitney Houston's 'I Will Always Love You' won which Grammy category at the 1994 ceremony?
questions.f: 'I Will Always Love You' won Record of the Year at the 36th Grammy Awards in 1994 — the category recognizes the performance and production of a specific recording, not the composition.

questions.q: Which Boyz II Men single earned the Grammy for Best R&B Performance by a Duo or Group at the 1995 ceremony?
questions.f: 'I'll Make Love to You' won Best R&B Performance by a Duo or Group at the 37th Grammy Awards in 1995 — Boyz II Men won the same category the year before for 'End of the Road.'

questions.q: Brandy and Monica won Grammy Best R&B Performance by a Duo or Group at the 1999 ceremony for which single?
questions.f: 'The Boy Is Mine' won Best R&B Performance by a Duo or Group at the 41st Grammy Awards in 1999 — the same ceremony dominated by Lauryn Hill.

questions.q: Soul Train — which inspired the Soul Train Music Awards — was created and hosted by which television pioneer?
questions.f: Don Cornelius created Soul Train in 1970 as a local Chicago broadcast before syndicating it nationally in 1971 — the show ran for 35 years and became the primary television platform for Black music.

questions.q: Which group won the Soul Train Music Award for Best R&B/Soul Group in 1993 for their debut 'Forever My Lady'?
Mariah Carey won Grammy Best New Artist at which year's ceremony?
Boyz II Men won Grammy Best R&B Performance by a Duo or Group in 1993 for which song?
The Soul Train Lady of Soul Award — honoring top female R&B performers — was inaugurated in which year?
Erykah Badu won Grammy Best Female R&B Vocal Performance at the 1998 ceremony for which debut single?
questions.f: Erykah Badu won Best Female R&B Vocal Performance at the 40th Grammy Awards in 1998 for 'On & On' — her debut single and the record that introduced neo-soul to a mainstream Grammy audience.

questions.q: At the 1999 Grammys where Lauryn Hill swept, Best Rap Solo Performance went to which artist for 'My Name Is'?
questions.f: 'My Name Is' won Best Rap Solo Performance at the 41st Grammy Awards in 1999 — Eminem's first Grammy win, announced the same night Lauryn Hill took five.

questions.q: Which R&B group won the American Music Award for Favorite Soul/R&B Band/Duo/Group for three consecutive years from 1993 to 1995?
questions.f: Boyz II Men won the AMA for Favorite Soul/R&B Band/Duo/Group three consecutive years from 1993 to 1995 — their commercial dominance of the early 90s reflected in the fan-voted format of the AMAs.

questions.q: Toni Braxton won Grammy Best R&B Album at the 1997 ceremony for which album?
questions.f: Secrets won Grammy Best R&B Album at the 39th Grammy Awards in 1997 — Toni Braxton had previously won the same category for her self-titled debut at the 37th ceremony in 1995.

questions.q: The Grammy for Best Rap Solo Performance in 1996 went to which rapper for 'Gangsta's Paradise'?
questions.f: Coolio's 'Gangsta's Paradise' — from the Dangerous Minds soundtrack — won Best Rap Solo Performance at the 38th Grammy Awards in 1996, beating Tupac Shakur's 'Dear Mama' in the same category.

questions.q: Mary J. Blige won Grammy Best R&B Album at the 38th ceremony in 1996 for which 1994 album?
The Grammy for Best R&B Song in 1997 went to which Babyface-written track from the 'Waiting to Exhale' soundtrack?
Which Grammy category did Toni Braxton win at the 1995 ceremony for 'Breathe Again'?
Mary J. Blige won Grammy Best Contemporary R&B Album at the 2000 ceremony — the first year the category existed. Which album earned her that inaugural award?
questions.f: Mary J. Blige's self-titled 1999 album 'Mary' won the inaugural Grammy for Best Contemporary R&B Album at the 42nd ceremony in 2000 — the first time the Recording Academy separated contemporary and traditional R&B.

questions.q: Soul Train began as a local Chicago broadcast in 1970 before going national in syndication in which year?
questions.f: Soul Train went to national syndication on October 2, 1971 — its first nationally broadcast episode aired in seven cities simultaneously, making it the first nationally syndicated Black-oriented music television show.

questions.q: Luther Vandross won Grammy Best R&B Vocal Performance — Male at the 1991 ceremony for which album?
Patti LaBelle won Grammy Best Traditional R&B Vocal Performance at the 1992 ceremony for which album?
Which artist had a 1995 debut smash with 'This Is How We Do It'?
questions.f: 'This Is How We Do It' spent seven weeks at #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1995 — Montell Jordan's commercial peak and one of the defining slow jams of the decade.

questions.q: Brian McKnight's career-defining 1999 ballad 'Back at One' appeared on which album?
questions.f: 'Back at One' peaked at #2 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1999 and earned Brian McKnight a Grammy nomination for Best Male R&B Vocal Performance.

questions.q: 112's debut single 'Cupid' (1996) appeared on which debut album?
questions.f: Room 112 was released on Puff Daddy's Bad Boy Entertainment in 1996 — 'Cupid' and 'Only You' established 112 as one of the label's defining slow jam acts.

questions.q: Which R&B singer had a 1998 debut hit with 'Sweet Lady' before starring in the Fast & Furious franchise?
questions.f: 'Sweet Lady' reached #1 on the Billboard R&B chart in 1998 — Tyrese Gibson's commercial debut before his acting career in the Fast & Furious franchise redefined his public identity.

questions.q: Next — the R&B trio behind 1997's 'Too Close' — were from which Midwestern city?
questions.f: 'Too Close' spent five weeks at #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1998 — Next's only major chart-topper, and one of the most recognizable slow jams of the late decade.

questions.q: Case's 1996 hit 'Touch Me Tease Me' from the Nutty Professor soundtrack featured which female rapper?
questions.f: 'Touch Me Tease Me' appeared on The Nutty Professor (1996) soundtrack — Foxy Brown's feature helped introduce both artists to a mainstream audience simultaneously.

questions.q: Brian McKnight — the slow jam architect behind Back at One — was born and raised in which upstate New York city?
questions.f: Brian McKnight was born in Buffalo, New York, where he grew up alongside his brother Claude McKnight of Take 6.

questions.q: Joe's 1997 major label breakthrough album 'All That I Am' was released on which label?
Which R&B female group featured 112 on their 1997 single 'All Cried Out'?
Next's 'Too Close' appeared on which 1997 debut album?
The Quiet Storm late-night radio format was pioneered by DJ Melvin Lindsey at which Washington D.C. radio station?
questions.f: DJ Melvin Lindsey launched the Quiet Storm format at WHUR-FM (Howard University's radio station) in 1976 — the format spread nationally through the early 1980s and became the primary home for R&B slow jams through the 90s.

questions.q: Tyrese Gibson was discovered as a teenager after appearing in a nationally broadcast commercial for which soft drink brand?
questions.f: Tyrese Gibson was discovered at age 16 after appearing in a 1994 Coca-Cola commercial — singing 'Always Coca-Cola' while riding a city bus. The ad launched his career and led directly to his record deal.

questions.q: Brian McKnight's brother Claude is a founding member of which celebrated Christian a cappella group?
questions.f: Claude McKnight co-founded Take 6 — the Grammy-winning Christian a cappella sextet — while his brother Brian McKnight pursued a secular R&B career, making the McKnight family one of the most musically accomplished in 90s gospel and R&B.

questions.q: Donell Jones's biggest single from his 1999 'Where I Wanna Be' album — which topped the Billboard R&B chart — was titled what?
questions.f: 'U Know What's Up' was Donell Jones's commercial peak — produced by Jones and Kyle West, it reached #1 on the Billboard R&B chart and crossed into the pop top 10 in 1999.

questions.q: Montell Jordan — before his 1995 breakthrough — attended which Malibu-based university on a basketball scholarship?
questions.f: Montell Jordan attended Pepperdine University in Malibu on a basketball scholarship before his music career — his six-foot-eight frame made him one of the more physically imposing figures in 90s R&B.

questions.q: The Quiet Storm radio format takes its name from a 1975 album by which Motown legend?
Kay Gee — a co-writer and producer associated with the Next camp — was a founding member of which New Jersey rap group?
Case's self-titled 1996 debut album was released on which Def Jam imprint?
The Quiet Storm radio format takes its name from a 1975 Smokey Robinson album released on which Motown imprint?
questions.f: Smokey Robinson's Quiet Storm was released on Tamla — one of Motown's several imprint labels — in 1975. DJ Melvin Lindsey named his WHUR-FM late-night format after the album the following year, and the format has never left radio since.

questions.q: Next — the Minneapolis trio behind 'Too Close' — released their debut on which independent label distributed through Arista?
questions.f: Next released Rated Next on Divine Mill Records — an independent imprint distributed through Arista — giving the Minneapolis trio major label reach through an indie structure that preserved their creative control.

questions.q: Allure — who featured 112 on 'All Cried Out' — were signed to which label?
Brian McKnight's 1992 self-titled debut — which contained 'One Last Cry' — was released on which label?
Which artist collaborated with God's Property on the massive 1997 crossover hit 'Stomp'?
questions.f: 'Stomp' was a watershed moment for 90s gospel, receiving massive airplay on secular MTV and R&B radio stations.

questions.q: Whitney Houston's 1996 album — the best-selling gospel album of all time — was the soundtrack to which movie?
questions.f: The Preacher's Wife remains the best-selling gospel album in history, moving an estimated 6 million copies worldwide.

questions.q: Which Minneapolis-based ensemble had a 1991 R&B crossover hit with 'Optimistic'?
questions.f: Sounds of Blackness blended traditional gospel with New Jack Swing, scoring a massive R&B chart hit with 'Optimistic'.

questions.q: Which sister-brother duo dominated the early 90s R&B charts with hits like 'Addictive Love' and 'I'll Take You There'?
questions.f: 'Addictive Love' spent two weeks at #1 on the Billboard Hot R&B Singles chart in 1991.

questions.q: Before becoming a Bad Boy Records star, which artist grew up singing in the church and directed the choir at her Newark, New Jersey parish?
questions.f: Faith Evans' heavy gospel vocal arrangements became the signature sonic backbone for early Bad Boy Records hits.

questions.q: Which R&B duo, originally part of the supergroup Jodeci, started their career performing in the gospel group Little Cedric and the Hailey Singers?
questions.f: Brothers Cedric and Joel Hailey released three gospel albums as Little Cedric and the Hailey Singers in the 1980s before joining Jodeci.

questions.q: Which female vocal duo released the breakthrough gospel-R&B crossover hit 'Shackles (Praise You)' in 2000?
CeCe Winans won a Grammy for Best Gospel Performance in 1996 for her duet with Whitney Houston on which song?
questions.f: 'Count on Me' — performed by Whitney Houston and CeCe Winans — appeared on the Waiting to Exhale soundtrack (1995). The song won the Grammy Award for Best Gospel Performance by a Duo, Group, Choir or Chorus at the 38th Grammy Awards in 1996.

questions.q: Which gospel star won a Grammy for her 1995 crossover duet 'Count On Me' with Whitney Houston?
Mase's 1997 hit 'Feel So Good' featured an iconic uncredited hook by which R&B singer with deep church roots?
Which secular hip-hop artist provided a famous guest verse on Kirk Franklin's 'Stomp'?
questions.f: Cheryl 'Salt' James of Salt-N-Pepa provided the guest rap verse, famously asking 'G.P. are you with me?'

questions.q: Which legendary R&B production duo signed and produced Sounds of Blackness for Perspective Records?
questions.f: Jam & Lewis co-founded Perspective Records with A&M and made Sounds of Blackness their flagship signing.

questions.q: Kirk Franklin's massive 1990s catalog was originally released on which influential independent gospel label?
questions.f: Founded by Vicki Mack Lataillade, GospoCentric Records launched Kirk Franklin's career before later partnering with major labels.

questions.q: Which R&B maestro wrote and produced the 1996 hit 'You Put a Move on My Heart' for Tamia, heavily featuring a massive gospel vocal arrangement?
questions.f: The song appeared on Quincy Jones's album Q's Jook Joint and introduced a young Tamia to the R&B world.

questions.q: Mary Mary's 2000 debut crossover hit 'Shackles (Praise You)' was produced by which architect of modern R&B and Gospel?
questions.f: Warryn Campbell produced the track and co-wrote it, establishing a production dynasty that bridged secular and gospel music.

questions.q: Mariah Carey and Boyz II Men's 'One Sweet Day' — which topped the Billboard Hot 100 for 16 consecutive weeks — appeared on which Mariah Carey album?
questions.f: 'One Sweet Day' appeared on Mariah Carey's fifth studio album 'Daydream,' released in October 1995. The song was written as a tribute to loved ones who had passed away. It spent 16 consecutive weeks at #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 — a record that stood until 2…

questions.q: Which Bad Boy producer created the gospel-tinged backing track for Faith Evans' 'Soon As I Get Home'?
Which gospel vocal arranger orchestrated the massive choir sound on Michael Jackson's 'Will You Be There'?
Which founding member of the R&B group Jodeci was originally a gospel organist who travelled the church circuit in North Carolina?
questions.f: Donald 'DeVante Swing' DeGrate played organ for gospel choirs before forming Jodeci.

questions.q: Which classic 1976 gospel track by the Clark Sisters was heavily sampled by Jay-Z on his 2001 track 'Family Affair'?
questions.f: Producer Just Blaze sampled 'Ha Ya (Eternal Life)' to create the backdrop for Jay-Z's 'Family Affair'.

questions.q: Which major 90s record label briefly ran a gospel imprint called 'B-Rite Music' which housed the group Trin-i-tee 5:7?
Which legendary gospel and a cappella artist co-produced the choir arrangements on Whitney Houston's 'The Preacher's Wife' soundtrack?
Which blockbuster single helped TLC's sophomore album 'CrazySexyCool' achieve Diamond status?
questions.f: 'Waterfalls' spent seven weeks at #1 in 1995, propelling 'CrazySexyCool' to become the best-selling album by an American girl group.

questions.q: Usher's sophomore album 'My Way' spawned his first Billboard Hot 100 #1 single. Which song was it?
questions.f: 'Nice & Slow' hit #1 in early 1998, establishing Usher as a global superstar after a relatively modest debut album.

questions.q: Destiny's Child's breakthrough sophomore album 'The Writing's on the Wall' featured which signature anthem?
questions.f: 'Say My Name' won two Grammy Awards and pushed the sophomore album to over 8 million copies sold in the US.

questions.q: Aaliyah completely redefined her sound on her sophomore album 'One In A Million' with which title track?
c: Age Ain't Nothing but a Number
questions.f: The title track 'One In A Million' peaked at #1 on the Billboard Mainstream R&B/Hip-Hop chart.

questions.q: Brandy's sophomore blockbuster 'Never Say Never' included a massive 13-week #1 duet with which fellow R&B star?
questions.f: 'The Boy Is Mine' was the lead single from Brandy's second album, making it the best-selling female duet in US chart history.

questions.q: Jagged Edge hit double-platinum with their sophomore album 'J.E. Heartbreak', which featured which massive wedding staple?
questions.f: 'Let's Get Married' reached #11 on the Hot 100, far surpassing any single from their debut album.

questions.q: Dru Hill's sophomore album 'Enter the Dru' featured which massive lead single?
Monica's sophomore album 'The Boy Is Mine' featured which solo #1 hit?
c: Don't Take It Personal (Just One of Dem Days)

questions.q: 112's sophomore album 'Room 112' contained which hit featuring Mase?
Ginuwine's sophomore album '100% Ginuwine' was anchored by which massive slow jam?
Boyz II Men's sophomore album 'II' debuted at #1 in 1994 and was distributed through which legendary Motown founder's company?
questions.f: Boyz II Men's sophomore album 'II' was released on Motown Records in 1994 — Berry Gordy's label distributed one of the decade's best-selling R&B albums, debuting at #1 on the Billboard 200.

questions.q: Timbaland and Missy Elliott took over production duties for Aaliyah's sophomore album, shifting her away from which debut producer?
questions.f: R. Kelly produced Aaliyah's entire debut album, but had no involvement in her sophomore release 'One In A Million'.

questions.q: 'The Writing's on the Wall' was the last Destiny's Child album to feature which original group member alongside Beyoncé and Kelly?
questions.f: LeToya Luckett and LaTavia Roberson left Destiny's Child shortly after the release of their sophomore album.

questions.q: Which prominent producer/writer co-wrote Brandy and Monica's 'The Boy Is Mine' for Brandy's sophomore album?
questions.f: Rodney 'Darkchild' Jerkins co-wrote and produced 'The Boy Is Mine', defining Brandy's sophomore sound.

questions.q: Dru Hill's sophomore album 'Enter the Dru' featured 'How Deep Is Your Love', which originally appeared on which film soundtrack?
questions.f: 'How Deep Is Your Love' served as the lead single for both the Rush Hour soundtrack and Dru Hill's sophomore album.

questions.q: D'Angelo's sophomore album 'Voodoo' was released on which label in 2000?
Which producer crafted Next's sophomore hit 'Wifey' from 'Welcome II Nextasy'?
Ginuwine's 'So Anxious' from his sophomore album featured background vocals from which frequent collaborator?
D'Angelo's sophomore album 'Voodoo' was heavily shaped by a collective of musicians known as what?
questions.f: The Soulquarians (including Questlove, James Poyser, and Pino Palladino) were instrumental in the Electric Lady Studios sessions for 'Voodoo'.

questions.q: TLC's 'Waterfalls' from their sophomore album 'CrazySexyCool' heavily interpolated the horn line from 'Listen to What the Man Said' by which original performing artist?
questions.f: The signature horn line in 'Waterfalls' is a direct interpolation of Paul McCartney & Wings' 1975 hit 'Listen to What the Man Said'.

questions.q: Aaliyah's Blackground Records label was founded by which music executive who was also her maternal uncle?
questions.f: Barry Hankerson — Aaliyah's uncle and former husband of Gladys Knight — founded Blackground Entertainment specifically to develop Aaliyah's career, giving her both family support and professional infrastructure.

questions.q: Jagged Edge's sophomore album — which contained their signature slow jam Let's Get Married — was titled what?
questions.f: J.E. Heartbreak (2000) was Jagged Edge's commercial breakthrough — produced largely by Jermaine Dupri, it went platinum and established the Atlanta quartet as slow jam royalty.

questions.q: Whitney Houston starred in and performed the iconic title track for which 1992 romantic thriller?
questions.f: The Bodyguard soundtrack remains the best-selling soundtrack album of all time, with over 44 million copies sold worldwide.

questions.q: Coolio's 1995 Grammy-winning mega-hit 'Gangsta's Paradise' (featuring L.V.) was the lead single for which Michelle Pfeiffer film?
questions.f: 'Gangsta's Paradise' spent 3 weeks at #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 and won the Grammy for Best Rap Solo Performance at the 1996 ceremony.

questions.q: The entire 1997 soundtrack for which Chicago-set family drama was written and produced solely by Babyface?
c: How Stella Got Her Groove Back
questions.f: The Soul Food soundtrack went platinum and introduced the supergroup Milestone — featuring Babyface, K-Ci & JoJo, and Kevon Edmonds — to mainstream audiences.

questions.q: The all-star anthem 'U Will Know' — featuring nearly every major male R&B voice of 1994 — was recorded for the soundtrack of which Houston-set film?
questions.f: 'U Will Know' featured Boyz II Men, Brian McKnight, Usher, R. Kelly, and over a dozen other R&B stars — and was co-written by a then-unknown D'Angelo.

questions.q: Which hip-hop artist collaborated with singer Nate Dogg for the 1994 hit 'Regulate' from the 'Above the Rim' soundtrack?
questions.f: 'Regulate' heavily sampled Michael McDonald's 'I Keep Forgettin'' and became one of the defining anthems of the G-Funk era.

questions.q: D'Angelo contributed 'Girl You Need to Change Your Mind' to the soundtrack of which 1996 Spike Lee film?
questions.f: D'Angelo's contribution to 'Get on the Bus' helped cement his credibility as a live-performance neo-soul artist beyond his debut album.

questions.q: The 1997 Soul Food film — whose soundtrack became a commercial hit — starred which actress in the lead role of Maxine Joseph?
questions.f: Soul Food (1997) starred Vivica A. Fox as Maxine Joseph alongside Nia Long and Vanessa L. Williams. The film was written and directed by George Tillman Jr. and grossed over $43 million at the US box office. Its soundtrack reached #2 on the Billboard 200.

questions.q: Coolio's 'Gangsta's Paradise' won which Grammy Award at the 38th ceremony in 1996?
questions.f: 'Gangsta's Paradise' won Best Rap Solo Performance at the 38th Grammy Awards in 1996. The song also won the MTV VMA for Video of the Year, making it one of the most award-decorated rap singles of the decade.

questions.q: Which artist provided the sultry 1996 hit 'Touch Me, Tease Me' (featuring Foxy Brown) for 'The Nutty Professor' soundtrack?
Tevin Campbell's hit 'I2I' (Eye to Eye) was prominently featured in which 1995 animated Disney film?
Total's breakthrough 'Can't You See' and other Bad Boy-adjacent acts appeared on 'New Jersey Drive Vol. 1' — distributed through which hip-hop label?
questions.f: New Jersey Drive Vol. 1 was distributed through Tommy Boy Records — primarily a hip-hop label — demonstrating how urban soundtracks of the mid-90s blurred genre lines.

questions.q: Destiny's Child recorded their debut single 'Killing Time' specifically for which 1997 sci-fi blockbuster soundtrack?
questions.f: 'Killing Time' predated the release of Destiny's Child's self-titled debut album and served as the world's introduction to the group.

questions.q: Total's 1995 breakthrough track 'Can't You See' (featuring The Notorious B.I.G.) debuted on which film's soundtrack?
questions.f: The song introduced Total as Bad Boy's flagship R&B girl group before their debut album even hit shelves.

questions.q: Which R&B supergroup—featuring Babyface, Kevon Edmonds, and K-Ci & JoJo—was formed strictly to record the track 'I Care 'Bout You' for the 'Soul Food' soundtrack?
questions.f: Milestone was a fictional group within the movie 'Soul Food', but the real-life R&B titans recorded the actual track for the official LaFace soundtrack.

questions.q: John Singleton's 1995 campus drama 'Higher Learning' featured a diverse rap and R&B soundtrack released on which major label?
questions.f: Higher Learning's Epic Records soundtrack included OutKast, Nas, Ice Cube, and Brandy — one of the most eclectic R&B-rap crossover compilations of the decade.

questions.q: Which producer crafted SWV's Wu-Tang remix of 'Anything' for the 'Above the Rim' soundtrack?
Lauryn Hill's Grammy-sweeping 1998 solo debut — which won five Grammy Awards including Album of the Year — was released on which record label?
questions.f: 'The Miseducation of Lauryn Hill' was released on Ruffhouse Records — a subsidiary of Columbia Records — on August 25, 1998. Ruffhouse was the label home of The Fugees, through which Lauryn Hill had already established her commercial credentials. The album so…

questions.q: Which hip hop artist's R&B-leaning track 'Phobia' appeared on the 1995 'Higher Learning' soundtrack?
The 'Above the Rim' soundtrack CD infamously excluded 'Pain', a fan-favorite hidden track (available only on cassette) by which West Coast legend?
questions.f: Death Row Records left 'Pain' off the original CD pressing of the soundtrack, making the cassette version a highly sought-after collector's item in the 90s.

questions.q: Which neo-soul pioneer co-wrote and co-produced the massive Black Men United supergroup anthem 'U Will Know' for the 'Jason's Lyric' soundtrack?
questions.f: Before dropping his debut album 'Brown Sugar', a young D'Angelo co-wrote and co-produced this anthem, which featured almost every major male R&B star of 1994.

questions.q: TLC contributed the song 'This Is How It Works' to the 'Waiting to Exhale' soundtrack. Who co-wrote and produced it?
D'Angelo's debut single 'Brown Sugar' (1995) peaked at which position on the Billboard Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs chart?
questions.f: D'Angelo's 'Brown Sugar' peaked at #5 on the Billboard Hot R&B/Hip-Hop Songs chart in 1995 and #27 on the Hot 100 — a strong showing for a neo-soul debut from an artist with no established mainstream lane.

questions.q: Which R&B group dominated hip-hop soul radio in 1996 with the Dr. Dre-featuring smash 'No Diggity'?
questions.f: 'No Diggity' spent three weeks at #1 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1996 and won the Grammy for Best R&B Performance by a Duo or Group — Blackstreet's commercial peak and one of the defining hip-hop soul records of the decade.

questions.q: Which legendary female MC opened the iconic hip-hop remix of Brandy's 'I Wanna Be Down'?
questions.f: The groundbreaking remix featured MC Lyte, Yo-Yo, and Queen Latifah, creating a definitive female empowerment anthem.

questions.q: The Notorious B.I.G. and which rising Bad Boy rapper provided the massive guest verses on the remix of 112's 'Only You'?
questions.f: The 'Only You' remix officially introduced Mase to a mainstream audience, launching his blockbuster Bad Boy career.

questions.q: SWV — whose 1993 'Right Here (Human Nature Remix)' became a hip-hop soul landmark — is an acronym standing for what?
questions.f: SWV — Sisters With Voices — formed in New York City in 1988. The trio of Coko, Lelee, and Taj became one of the defining acts of the hip-hop soul era.

questions.q: Mariah Carey's 1996 hip-hop soul ballad 'Breakdown' featured which Ohio rap trio?
questions.f: 'Breakdown' from Mariah's Daydream album featured Bone Thugs-n-Harmony — an unexpected but seamless pairing that demonstrated how fully hip-hop and R&B had merged by 1996.

questions.q: The Notorious B.I.G. featured on the Bad Boy debut single of which female R&B trio — the track that introduced them to mainstream audiences in 1995?
questions.f: 'Can't You See' debuted on the New Jersey Drive Vol. 1 soundtrack in 1995 — Total's introduction to mainstream audiences and one of Bad Boy's earliest hip-hop soul crossover moments.

questions.q: Which female R&B trio broke through in 1994 with the Denzil Foster-produced hip-hop soul ballad 'If You Love Me'?
questions.f: Brownstone's 'If You Love Me' — produced by Denzil Foster and Thomas McElroy — became one of 1994's defining slow jam crossover records, reaching #8 on the Billboard Hot 100.

questions.q: Kelly Price's massive 'Friend of Mine' remix featured R. Kelly alongside which legendary soul singer?
Xscape's hip-hop soul debut — which launched the Jermaine Dupri-produced group in 1993 — was titled what?
questions.f: Xscape's debut album Hummin' Comin' at 'Cha (1993) was produced by Jermaine Dupri and introduced the Atlanta quartet as one of So So Def's flagship hip-hop soul acts.

questions.q: Horace Brown's 1996 'One for the Money' remix prominently featured an early guest verse from which rap mogul?
Which NYC-based production duo, known collectively as the Trackmasters, dominated the R&B remix era for artists like Mariah Carey and Mary J. Blige?
questions.f: Jean-Claude 'Poke' Olivier and Samuel 'Tone' Barnes (The Trackmasters) were the defining architects of the glossy 90s hip-hop soul remix sound.

questions.q: Jodeci's 'Freek'n You' received a gritty 'Mr. Dalvin's Freek Mix' featuring which two members of the Wu-Tang Clan?
questions.f: The rugged remix became a massive street anthem, proving that Jodeci's sound could seamlessly integrate with the hardest NYC hip-hop.

questions.q: Janet Jackson's 'Got 'til It's Gone' received the legendary 'Ummah Jay Dee's Revenge Mix', produced by which Detroit hip-hop icon?
questions.f: J Dilla (then known as Jay Dee) crafted the official remix under his Ummah production collective moniker.

questions.q: The 'Hip Hop Mix' of Boyz II Men's 'Vibin'' featured Craig Mack, Busta Rhymes, Method Man, and which Naughty By Nature frontman?
questions.f: The 'New Flava' mix was a posse-cut remix that successfully bridged the gap between smooth Philadelphia harmony and rugged East Coast rap.

questions.q: Next's massive 1998 hit 'Too Close' was built around the groove from 'Christmas Rappin'' by which hip-hop pioneer?
questions.f: Producer Kay Gee looped Kurtis Blow's 1979 classic 'Christmas Rappin'' to create the instrumental for 'Too Close'.

questions.q: Faith Evans' 1998 anthem 'Love Like This' was built on a massive loop of 'Chic Cheer' by which legendary 70s band?
Blackstreet's iconic 'No Diggity' famously sampled 'Grandma's Hands' by which soul legend?
The '6th Borough Remix' of Groove Theory's 'Tell Me' featured a guest verse from which New York rap group?
D'Angelo's 'Brown Sugar' received a gritty, underground hip-hop remix produced by which legendary Gang Starr member?
questions.f: DJ Premier's remix stripped away the lush neo-soul instrumentation, placing D'Angelo's vocals over a raw, signature boom-bap beat.

questions.q: Mary J. Blige's 'Love No Limit' Puff Daddy remix famously anchored its groove on a sample of 'Risin' to the Top' by which 80s artist?
questions.f: Keni Burke's 1982 bassline from 'Risin' to the Top' is one of the most sampled grooves in hip-hop and R&B history.

questions.q: Timbaland's production on Ginuwine's debut 'Pony' defined the hip-hop soul sound for 1997 — what was that debut album titled?
questions.f: Ginuwine...the Bachelor (1997) was produced almost entirely by Timbaland — its futuristic drum programming and minimalist hip-hop soul arrangements established a new aesthetic that influenced a decade of R&B production.

questions.q: Michael Jackson's 'Remember The Time' received a house/R&B 'Silky Soul 7' remix produced by which Chicago house pioneer?
Which 1988 Bobby Brown album — selling over seven million copies in the US — is considered the commercial peak of New Jack Swing?
questions.f: Don't Be Cruel debuted at #1 on the Billboard 200 in 1988 and spawned five Top 10 singles including 'My Prerogative,' 'Don't Be Cruel,' and 'Every Little Step.' It remains the defining commercial artifact of the New Jack Swing era.

questions.q: Which Bobby Brown anthem, produced by Teddy Riley, became the ultimate New Jack Swing declaration of independence in 1988?
questions.f: The track hit #1 on the Billboard Hot 100, cementing Bobby Brown's status as a solo megastar after leaving New Edition.

questions.q: Keith Sweat's 1987 debut single 'I Want Her' — widely considered one of the first major New Jack Swing records — appeared on which debut album?
c: I'll Give All My Love to You
